$comment: GH-642 (queue item 6, stage 0b) - THE ONE LIST OF WHAT A CALCULATION NEEDS.
The owner's decision, 23.09.2026: 'there will be a list of the input parameters we
need for the calculation. The wizard will look at it, the calculation will look at
it, so that we do not put different checks in different places.'
ONE FILE, ONE READER. The server reads this; the wizard, Settings, the run and the
incomplete-run panel get it parsed, the way `analysis-result.schema.json` is already
read by the server and never copied into `assets`. A second list is the drift this
file exists to remove.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND DELIBERATELY:
- 'what breaks without it'. Who reads an input is what the dependency graph says;
restating it here would be a second answer to that question.
- the readings of a sample, one by one. Their names are declared once, by the lab
name map (`sample-manager.js`, `readingKeysFor`); an entry points at it.
- anything derived rather than asked: the climate regime, the purpose, the time
zone, the effective species. Those are named in `derived` below so the equality
test can exclude them BY NAME, with a reason, instead of by a rule.
`storedAs` SAYS AT WHICH PATH, when the config path is not the input's own key. GH-777, the
reviewer's return: `storedIn: config` alone was not enough, because the reader walked the KEY as
a path and six inputs are written elsewhere - `schedule.efficiency` lands in
`irrigation.efficiency`, `soil.moisture` and `turf.rootDepth` and the three Clegg readings in
`traffic.schedule.*`, the two LED fields in `turf.led.*`. Measured on the stand: 3 sites carry an
irrigation efficiency and 2 a soil moisture, and every one of them was reported to its own owner
as not entered. The paths are read from the writers in `assets/settings-init.js`; absent
`storedAs`, the key IS the path.
`storedIn` SAYS WHERE THE VALUE LIVES WHEN IT EXISTS, and it is a different fact from
`filledIn`, which says where a PERSON enters it. GH-777 (queue item 4): the server records
what a site had when a run started, and it was reading the site's config for every input -
so an input stored elsewhere came out 'not filled' and the client was told it had not
entered a value it had entered. Measured on the stand: 5 of 21 sites carry
`sites.soil_texture_override` in the column, and 2 sites carry their PGR application only in
the spray log. Blame on the client is the worst direction for an error, so the storage is
declared here and read by name: `config`, `siteColumn`, `sprayLog`, `sampleSet`. An empty
list means nothing stores it, and the guard holds that against `filledIn` in both
directions - an input nobody fills is an input nothing stores, and a storage with no reader
on the server is red on the day it is declared.
`required: null` MEANS THE OWNER HAS NOT DECIDED, and it travels with `decision`.
It is not a guess and not a default: a warning built from this list stays silent
about such an input until she answers.
Contents drafted by the analyst (`PLAN-calculation-inputs-RU.md`, sections 14 and
14a) from a reading of the tree and the database, 22-24.09.2026.

$commentWhenAbsent: GH-749 (queue item 3ay) - WHAT THE ABSENCE OF A READING COSTS, declared beside the reading
rather than written into each module that meets it. A pair is {input, effect}: the key is one
of the read spellings this entry already declares, and each effect is one thing that does not
happen without it. The guard holds the pairs the code records against these, both ways -- a
pair recorded and not declared is red, and a pair declared that no module records is red --
and every declared pair has a case that runs the module and reads the pair back.
THESE ARE NOT THE WORDS A CLIENT READS. They name the effect for a reader of the run's own
record; the sentence a person sees is the owner's and is a separate question.
AND A PAIR SAYS WHAT IT DOES, NOT WHAT SOMETHING ELSE DOES. The pH pair used to read `the
phosphorus floor is not adjusted by pH`, which is a statement about how MLSN and SLAN behave -
parked as an open question by the owner's decision of 25.09.2026, and not this record's to
assert. The wording names the absence and the fact that a module recorded it; what any
methodology then does with a missing reading is that methodology's own subject.
A REQUIRED SETTING HAS NO PAIR HERE, and that is the analyst's decision rather than an
omission: `turf.methodology` has one owner and no allowed absence, so the resolver REFUSES
instead of recording an effect -- an effect would admit the case as an allowed one.

The sentence a client reads is `{Module} was not calculated because {label} has not been entered.
Add it in {place}.` -- the owner's form, approved 24.09.2026. `filledIn` carries the KEY of a place;

The wizard's steps are deliberately absent: a person does not go back to them (the analyst's 49.3).
Words drafted by the analyst from the tab buttons of `settings.blade.php` and `data.blade.php`, and
they are hers to change without a line of code changing.
GH-644 - names the run reads out of its own state that are NOT inputs. Each one
with what it is, because 'read but not in the list' has two very different
meanings and only one of them is a defect: a result another engine wrote, or a
fact derived from an input. Anything read and in neither this block nor the list
is an input nobody declared, and the equality test names it.
notInputs.turf.ambientDLI: a result: the shade engine returns it in its own output -- `assets/shade-engine.js` / `gssh_shade_engine`, and the run carries it into the next pass at `assets/hub-tissue-v3.js` / `gaip_carryRunComputedInto`
notInputs.turf.dli: a result: the cascade's shade engine produces it, declared as the output `computed.shade.dli` by `assets/dependency-graph.json` / `computed.shade.dli` and executed at `assets/cascade-orchestrator.js` / `executeShadeEngine`
notInputs.turf.shade: a result: the same engine's whole shade block, declared as the output `computed.shade` -- `assets/cascade-orchestrator.js` / `executeShadeEngine`
notInputs.soil.ESP: a result: worked out from the sodium and the CEC -- `assets/hub-tissue-v3.js` / `assessSoilSodium`
notInputs.climate.data: a result: the climate block the run fetches and stores each pass -- `assets/hub-orchestrator.js` / `getAuthoritativeClimate`
notInputs.site.hemisphere: derived from the latitude, one comparison -- `assets/shade-orchestrator.js` / `_onClimateReady`
notInputs.site.region: derived from the coordinates -- `assets/hub-orchestrator.js` / `detectRegion`. Measured under GH-712: the derivation exists in ten files under that name, and this is the one in the run's own path
notInputs.location.region: derived from the coordinates, the same derivation as `site.region` -- `assets/hub-orchestrator.js` / `detectRegion`; the places that name `location.region` read it and none writes it
notInputs.site.ledAvailable: a result: whether the lighting step found any lamp hours -- `assets/hub-tissue-v3.js` / `ledAvailable: o > 0`
notInputs.pgr.gddThreshold: derived from the PGR product type, a property of the product rather than a question -- `assets/gilba-pgr-module-v3.js` / `w_pure`
notInputs.climate.historical: a result: the historical weather window the run fetches from the PGR application date and carries into the next pass (GH-589) -- `assets/hub-tissue-v3.js` / `gaip_carryRunComputedInto`
notInputs.turf.ambientDLISource: derived: which road the ambient DLI came by, returned beside `turf.ambientDLI` -- `assets/shade-engine.js` / `gssh_shade_engine`
notInputs.water.SAR: BOTH A LAB COLUMN AND A COMPUTED VALUE, measured under GH-712 and narrower than the reason written earlier the same night: a water report may carry SAR itself -- `assets/lab-import.js` / `SAR: { min: 0, max: 100, unit: '' }` -- and it is also computed from the ions where no column supplied it -- `assets/word-export.js` / `data.water.SAR = Na_meq`. Because a person's report can supply it, calling it purely a result is wrong; which class it belongs to is not settled here
notInputs.water.adjSAR: a result: the Suarez adjusted SAR, computed from the ions -- `assets/soil-structure-engine.js` / `calcSuarezAdjSAR`
notInputs.soil.meq: a result: the milliequivalent cations the sample layer derives from the sample's own ppm values -- `assets/sample-manager.js` / `meq: { K: K_me, Ca: Ca_me, Mg: Mg_me, Na: Na_me }`
notInputs.turf.growthMultiplier: a result: the combined growth modifier the stress engine wrote, read back when the wear inputs are built -- `assets/hub-orchestrator.js` / `buildWearRecoveryInputs`
notInputs.site.country: READ BY TWO ENGINES AND FILLED BY NOTHING, measured under GH-725: `assets/gilba-hub-v2.js` / `country: null` is the only place it is set, so both readers always see null -- `assets/ambient-dli-engine.js` / `detectRegion(lat, lon, state?.site?.country)`, where it is only an alternative to a coordinate box. GH-727 left it with that one reader: the pre-emergent builder keyed a New Zealand branch on it, and it now asks the site's own coordinates by id instead. Whether it should be asked for is not settled here

derived.turf.pgrActive: from the last PGR application in the spray journal and the window the PGR engine owns (`GAIP_PGR.isInUse`, ninety days), assembled by `assets/hub-tissue-v3.js` / `gaip_transformToCascadeFormat`. GH-780 (queue item 3vc) moved it off `pgr.enabled`, the switch the owner removed on 29.09.2026: there is no switch, and a site is using a PGR when its journal says so. Three answers, not two: an application inside the window is `true`, one outside it or none at all is `false` -- the journal is the complete record -- and no answer from the journal is `null`, so the shade advice neither asserts nor denies a conflict.
